## Git remotes

Remote repositories are versions of your project that are hosted on the Internet or network somewhere.

Collaborating with others involves managing these remote repositories and pushing and pulling data to and from them when you need to share work.

::: {.row}
::: {.pill .pill-lg .p-orange}
GitHub
:::

::: {.pill .pill-lg .p-tan}
GitLab
:::

::: {.pill .pill-lg .p-salmon}
Bitbucket
:::
:::

## GitHub

- AI-powered developer platform that allows developers to create, store, manage and share their code.
- It provides the distributed version control of Git plus access control, bug tracking, software feature requests, task management, continuous integration, and wikis for every project.
- It is the world's largest source code host.

## Remote and local repositories

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-align: center
flowchart LR
  L1["Local computer"] -- "push" --> R(["Remote"])
  R -- "fetch / pull" --> L1
  L2["Local computer"] -- "push" --> R
  R -- "fetch / pull" --> L2
  L3["Local computer"] -- "push" --> R
  R -- "fetch / pull" --> L3
```

## SSH connection

Secure Shell (SSH) is a cryptographic network protocol for operating network services securely over an unsecured network by providing a secure channel to connect an SSH client with an SSH server.
